newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria oil chief urges local firms to invest.
newsitem.headline: Algeria oil chief urges local firms to invest.

text.p: The head of Algeria's state-owned energy firm Sonatrach on Tuesday offered local companies lucrative slices in a multi-billion-dollar plan to help develop the country's oil and gas resources.

"The range of Sonatrach's development plan and the gigantic resources needed to achieve this are a formidable task and a challenge. I invite you to come and share them with us," Nazim Zouioueche told industrialists gathered in Algiers to take a first-hand look at the firm's plans over the next five years.
Among those attending the meeting were senior managers of oil and gas-related local companies, Sider, Anabib and GTP, already working as subcontractors in development projects with Sonatrach.
"Sonatrach is open to all forms of partnership with national companies," said Zouioueche, quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS.
He said Sonatrach's five-year development programme ran into "several billion dollars." Other Algerian energy officials have put the cost at about $17 billion.

Among the projects forming the development plan are buidling gas and oil facilities, including a pipeline carrying gas from fields in the far south of Algeria to Hassi R'Mel, the main gas field and gas gathering center.
Zouioueche later told Algerian state-run radio that his company's aim in working in partnership with local and foreign firms was to cut costs and boost profits.

Since last year, Sonatrach has struck several contracts with foreign companies including British Petroleum, Arco, Agip, Total and Repsol to develop oil and gas projects. They include pipelines and the development of huge fields such as Hassi Berkine.
The oil and gas sector accounot for more than 90 percent of Algeria's total exports.
The value of its oil and gas exports rose to $12.6 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from the previous year thanks to improved efficiency and higher international oil prices.
Algeria plans to raise annual earnings to about $16 billion by the year 2000 due mainly to increased gas exports.
